- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) and forecast shows a sharp downward move, adjust downward bias by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.23) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast peak by 5–15% to prevent overshoot after spikes.  
- For 30-day horizons, if recent 18-day history shows strong upward trend, model tends to overestimate; apply mean reversion correction by subtracting 2–5% from forecasted peak.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive sentiment (≥ 0.53) over 3+ days, model often overestimates; apply downward bias to 3rd–5th day of forecast horizon.  
- If forecast shows early sharp decline (first 3–5 days) and sentiment is neutral or negative, expect true outcome to rebound; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in reversal.  
- For 30-day forecasts with high volatility, reduce forecast variance by 10–15% if sentiment is mixed or trending sideways.
